The objective is this document is to explore the diversity and interconnectedness of [FRB CESAB projects](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/about-the-foundation/le-cesab/) using network analysis. The exploration consists of two complementary analysis:   

1. Project cesabhip network based on who is collaborating in the projects   

1.1. Cesab cesabhip network based on the authors of Cesab publications and their external collaborators

2. Citation coupling network based on the scientific articles published by projects

3. Getting thematic information : topics, fields, keywords from OpenAlex, for each Cesab publication



```{r}
library(zoteror)
library(igraph)
library(visNetwork)
library(plotly)
library(bibliometrix) # to build citation networks

devtools::load_all()


in_data <- here::here("data", "raw-data", "cesab")
out_data <- here::here("data", "derived-data")

## Import the liste of Cesab members to cross with the list of authors
cesab <- read.csv2(here::here(out_data, "cesab_members.csv"))
cesab$group %>% unique() # 73 groups in total


# remove guest and stagiaire
cesab <- cesab[!cesab$function_in_group %in% c("Guest", "Stagiaire"), ]

# remove non active members (and keep NA)
cesab <- cesab[!cesab$still_member %in% 0, ]

# add a column with merged Liastname and Firtsname
cesab$name <- paste(cesab$lastname, cesab$firstname, sep = " ")

# remove duplicates (mostly for Pelagic 1 and 2)
cesab <- cesab[!duplicated(cesab[, c("group", "name")]), ]

infoV <- tapply(cesab$group, cesab$name, paste, collapse = "<br>")

nmem <- table(cesab$group)
nproj <- table(table(cesab$name))

nmem <- table(cesab$group)
nproj <- table(table(cesab$name))
# summary(as.numeric(table(cesab$group)))
# # table(duplicated(cesab))
# nrow(cesab) # 1015 cesabhip

# citation dataset
M <- readRDS(file.path(out_data, "cesab_bibliometrix.rds"))

M$shorttitle <- substr(firstup(M$display_name), 1, 30)
M$breaktitle <- breaks_string(firstup(M$display_name))
M$linkDOI <- paste0(
  "<a href=\'",
  paste0("https://www.doi.org/", M$DI),
  "\'>",
  M$DI,
  "</a>"
)
```




The FRB-Cesab hosted```r length(nmem)```  projects between ```r min(cesab$start_year)``` and ```r max(cesab$start_year)``` with ```r length(unique(cesab$name))``` different researchers. On average, a CESAB project includes ```r round(mean(nmem), 1)``` cesab, with a minimum of ```r  min(nmem)``` for ```r names(which.min(nmem))``` and a maximum of ```r  max(nmem)``` for ```r names(which.max(nmem))``` (@tbl-mempro). Most researchers participated in a single project (N=```r nproj["1"]```), but ```r nproj["2"]``` researchers collaborated in two projects; and ```r sum(nproj[-(1:2)])``` researchers worked on three or more projects.  



```{r}
#| label: tbl-mempro
#| tbl-cap: "Number of cesab, principal investigators (PI), and post-doc per CESAB project."
#| 
table(cesab$group, cesab$function_in_group)
```

### Bipartite cesabhip network

```{r}
#| label: fig-bimem
#| fig-cap: "Simplified bipartite network containing all projects (nodes in blue square) and the cesab that participated in multiple projects (nodes in red circle)."
#| 
netBI <- graph_from_data_frame(
  cesab[, c("name", "group")]
)
V(netBI)$type <- V(netBI)$name %in% cesab$group

V(netBI)$color <- ifelse(V(netBI)$type, "blue", "red")
V(netBI)$shape <- ifelse(V(netBI)$type, "square", "dot")
# V(netBI)$size <- ifelse(V(netBI)$type, 3, 1)

extra <- ifelse(
  V(netBI)$type,
  "",
  infoV[match(V(netBI)$name, names(infoV))]
)
V(netBI)$title <- paste(
  V(netBI)$name,
  extra,
  sep = "<br>"
)

# remove cesab that are not connected to multiple groups
# for visualization purpose only
showBI <- delete_vertices(netBI, degree(netBI) == 1)

visNetwork::visIgraph(
  showBI,
  randomSeed = 25,
  layout = "layout_with_fr", #layout_with_kk, layout_nicely
  smooth = TRUE
) |>
  visOptions(
    highlightNearest = TRUE
  )
```

The bipartite network offer a complete visualization of the projects (blue square) and their cesab (red circles). However, the complexity of handling two types of nodes (project and member) prevent further in-depth analysis.



## Cesab colaboration network

The idea is to extract all authors from the Cesab publication list, distinguish 2 groups based on whether or not authors are part of a Cesab group, and get an idea of colaborations outside of Cesab.

Code to get the Cesab publication list and define which authors are Cesab members and which ones are exterior.
```{r}

## Get the list of Cesab publications and remove Core
cesab_pub <- zoteror::get_zotero_data("~/Zotero")
df <- cesab_pub |> dplyr::filter(
  collection != "_Core",
  category %in% c("bookSection", "journalArticle"),
  !is.na(doi)
)

## Clean the author names
df <- df |> 
  dplyr::select(collection, year, category, author, journal, doi)

## homogenize full names by keeping the last name and reducing all remaining into initials

# keep original names too
original_names <- sapply(df$author, function(x){x |> stringr::str_split(" ; ")})

initials <- function(name) {
  surname <- stringr::str_extract(name, "^[^,]+") # everything before comma
  firstname   <- stringr::str_extract(name, "(?<=,\\s).*") # everything after comma + whitespace

  init <- firstname |>
    stringr::str_extract_all("[A-Z]", simplify = TRUE) |> # extract all capital letters as a matrix
    paste(collapse = " ")

  paste(surname, init)
}


# apply initials function to each line au co-authors from the publication df:
authors <- sapply(df$author, function(x){
  x |>
  stringr::str_split(" ; ") |>
  unlist() |>
  purrr::map_chr(initials) |>
  purrr::map_chr(clean_string)
})

# Put df in long format such that for a given article, 1 author = 1 line
authors <- lapply(1: length(authors), function(x){
  tab <- data.frame(
    doi = df$doi[[x]],
    collection = df$collection[[x]],
    category = df$category[[x]],
    author = original_names[[x]],
    author_simple = authors[[x]])
    rownames(tab) <- NULL
  return(tab)
}) 

# make dataframe from list
authors <- do.call(rbind, authors)

# add simplified author names to long df
df <- dplyr::left_join(
  df |> dplyr::select(-author),
  authors
)

# now try this with the members names:
cesab$names_simple <- paste(cesab$lastname, cesab$firstname, sep = ", ")
cesab$names_simple <- sapply(cesab$names_simple, initials) |>
  sapply(X = _, clean_string)

# add column is_cesab
df$is_cesab <- ifelse(
  df$author_simple %in% cesab$names_simple,
  TRUE, FALSE
)



```

Code to build the network:
```{r}
# create a bipartite graph of authors, link if co-authors
net_coauth <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  df[, c("author_simple", "doi")]
) 


# distinguish cesab members (TRUE), and external (FALSE)
V(net_coauth)$is_cesab <- ifelse(
  V(net_coauth)$name %in% cesab$names_simple,
  TRUE, FALSE
)

# assign blue dots to cesab members, red dots to external, green squares for papers
V(net_coauth)$color <- ifelse(V(net_coauth)$name %in% cesab$names_simple, "blue", "red")
V(net_coauth)$color[which(V(net_coauth)$name %in% df$doi)] <- "green"
V(net_coauth)$shape <- ifelse(V(net_coauth)$name %in% df$doi, "square", "dot")

```

The full network with verticies representing papers (DOIs) and authors contains 2822 nodes and 4930 links. 

Use Romain's technique to remove edges when there is only 1 connection (to limit the edges within Cesab groups) --> reduce to 1278 nodes and 3386 edges.

```{r}

# simplify network and remove unique links
net_c <- delete_vertices(net_coauth, degree(net_coauth) == 1)
E(net_c)$arrow.mode <- 0


visNetwork::visIgraph(
  net_c,
  randomSeed = 25,
  layout = "layout_with_fr", #layout_with_kk, layout_nicely
  smooth = TRUE
) |>
  visNetwork::visOptions(
    highlightNearest = TRUE
  )

```

Still very messy. Try bipartite projection in order to onty see the authors, who should be linked if the are co-authors.

But this puzzles me !
```{r}

V(net_coauth)$type <- V(net_coauth)$name %in% df$author_simple
split_coauth <- bipartite_projection(net_coauth, multiplicity = TRUE)

split_coauth
```



### Openalex : retrieve fields and keywords

Here I wanted to look at the information we could get out of OPenAlex to see if it would be useful to the run a LLM on it or classify this information in some way and get a sense of the evolution of Cesab thematics over time.


```{r}
options(openalexR.mailto = "camille.coux@fondationbiodiversite.fr")

dois <- unique(cesab_pub$doi)[1:10]

res <- openalexR::oa_fetch(
  entity  = "works",
  doi     = dois,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Explore topics
topics_df <- res |>
  dplyr::select(doi, topics) |>
  tidyr::unnest(topics) |>
  dplyr::select(doi, i, type, display_name) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = display_name)


topics_df

```

```{r}

topics <- unique(topics_df$topic)
topics
subfield <- unique(topics_df$subfield)
subfield
field <- unique(topics_df$field)
field
```

```{r}

# explore keywords

keywords_df <- res |>
  dplyr::select(doi, keywords) |>
  tidyr::unnest(keywords)

kw_ex <- keywords_df |>
  dplyr::filter(doi ==  "https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.13201") |>
  dplyr::select(display_name) |> 
  as.vector()

table(keywords_df$doi) |> as.vector()
```


```{r}

# explore concepts

concepts_df <- res |>
  dplyr::select(doi, concepts) |>
  tidyr::unnest(concepts)

concepts_ex <- concepts_df |>
  dplyr::filter(doi ==  "https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.13201") |>
  dplyr::select(display_name) |> 
  as.vector()

concepts_ex
```
